guide: Open Start and type your organization name, the value of one volunteer hour (your own setting), the days a volunteer counts as new and the hours that decide a call or a letter.
List every volunteer on Volunteers with a role, joined date, status and availability; hours worked, last shift and days since fill in from the shift log.
Add the planned shifts of the coming weeks to Shift Slots with the people needed and signed up; the gap fills in.
Record each shift in Shifts Worked as worked, no-show or booked; Hours by Volunteer, Hours by Program and Month and Hours Value fill in.
Type the shift IDs of the next days into Tomorrow's Shifts and the IDs of open slots into Gaps by Date to get the reminders and the next person to ask.
Type the IDs of lapsed volunteers into Lapsed Volunteers and of volunteers who also give into Volunteers Who Also Give.
If you run memberships, list members on Members, record each payment on Dues Payments and type the IDs of members to renew into Renewals Due; switch the pages off on Membership Switch if you do not.
Set the share of members who renew (your estimate) on Membership Switch and read Dues Forecast for the next 12 months.
Use the 18 tools for decisions: gaps, fill planning, reminders, matching, value, lapsed volunteers, recruitment, renewals and dues.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Read the Volunteers and Members Dashboard and the charts every week.
A founder with volunteers and no staff can use the same sheets with one program and a short list of volunteers; start with Volunteers, Shift Slots and Shifts Worked.

listing.title: Nonprofit Volunteer and Membership Tracker Excel Template: Shifts, Hours, Lapsed Volunteers, Dues, Renewals
listing.headline: Fill every shift, keep your volunteers and renew your members
listing.description:
Run the people side of a small community nonprofit in one Excel workbook. Built for a volunteer coordinator, an executive director or a founder with volunteers and no staff who must fill shifts, remind volunteers, keep them coming back and renew members. Volunteers holds the roster with role, availability and status. Shift Slots shows the people needed against signed up, and Gaps by Date ranks the open shifts by date, names the busiest week and the volunteer to ask first. Shifts Worked records every shift, and Hours by Volunteer, Hours by Program and Month and Hours Value turn it into hours and into value at your own setting for one volunteer hour.

Lapsed Volunteers ranks people who stopped coming by the hours they gave and sets a step: call, write or let go. Volunteers Who Also Give joins the roster to your donor book. The membership side holds Members, Dues Payments, Member Levels, Renewals Due and a 12-month Dues Forecast with your renewal rate, and it can be switched off. 18 tools answer the weekly questions: the shift gap finder, the fill planner, the availability matcher, the reminder list, the value calculator, the lapsed ranker, recruitment need, the renewal rate check and the dues forecast with Base, Best and Worst. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to volunteers, members and staff.

This is part six of the Nonprofit Organization suite. It works in Excel and Google Sheets, has no macros and no subscription, and comes with a demo copy full of sample data. Forecasts and verdicts are your own estimate, not a promise. It helps you keep records and is not accounting or legal advice; ask your accountant what your own rules need.

Members at this level who have not lapsed: {col:members.level_n}. Yearly dues of those members: {col:members.level_dues}.
Member on this page: {col:members.member}, ID {col:members.member_id}, status {col:members.status}, due {col:members.due_date}.
Print one page for each level and attach the list of members at that level.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own organization and check your local rules.
